tools.name: whoami
tools.description:
Which account this connection is, and what it may do: signed in with a Studio MCP key or anonymous,
    the row cap, and whether a model key is available for plain-English requests.

tools.name: plan_dataset
tools.description:
See the tables, sizes and relationships the engine would build, before any rows exist. Free (no
    rows are made), so it is worth calling before generate_dataset on anything non-trivial: review
    what it understood and assumed, then adjust your request or schema before spending a real call.

tools.name: generate_dataset
tools.description:
Make a verified relational dataset and wait for it: every foreign key checked, dates correctly
    ordered, declared aggregates and rates exact, before anything is returned. Deterministic for a seed.

    Use this when you give a `schema` or `ddl` (seconds). For a plain-English `request` the engine

tools.name: start_generation
tools.description:
Start a generation in the background and return a job_id at once. Use it for any plain-English
    `request` (a model designs the tables, which takes minutes) — then call get_status(job_id) every
    20-30 seconds until it says done. Arguments are the same as generate_dataset.

    Returns:

tools.name: get_status
tools.description:
Where a start_generation job is. While running: the stage it is in and how long it has run. When
    done: the same answer generate_dataset returns (dataset_id, verification, tables, certificate).

tools.name: cancel_generation
tools.description: Stop a running start_generation job. It stops at the next stage boundary and keeps nothing.

tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description:
The full certificate for a dataset made by generate_dataset: every claim (stated vs actual),
    every requirement's status and evidence, realism findings, planted defects/anomalies if any, and
    the pattern charts. This is the whole answer key, not the trimmed form generate_dataset returns.

tools.name: query_dataset
tools.description:
